1	/**
2	 * Plain-text extraction from Markdown for FTS5 indexing.
3	 *
4	 * Canonical implementation. Previously duplicated across:
5	 *   - routes/admin.ts        (re-index from R2 / DB)
6	 *   - routes/docs.ts         (POST /docs body indexing)
7	 *   - routes/import.ts       (single import body indexing)
8	 *   - routes/import-bulk.ts  (bulk import body indexing)
9	 *
10	 * The 4 copies were behaviourally equivalent but cosmetically
11	 * diverged (comments, blank lines, `text = ...; return text;` vs
12	 * `return text.replace(...);`). A real bug fix in one wouldn't
13	 * propagate. Extracted here on 2026-05-18 so all 4 call sites
14	 * stay aligned.
15	 *
16	 * The regex chain is intentionally lossy — FTS5 doesn't need
17	 * markdown syntax preserved, just searchable plain text:
18	 *   - Code blocks: dropped entirely (FTS5 wouldn't tokenize them
19	 *     usefully anyway)
20	 *   - Inline code: keep the content, drop backticks
21	 *   - Images: keep alt text only (the URL never matches a search)
22	 *   - Links: keep the visible text, drop the URL
23	 *   - Wikilinks `[[ref]]`: keep the ref
24	 *   - Markdown markers (headings, bold, italic, lists, quotes, hr):
25	 *     dropped
26	 *   - Whitespace collapsed to single spaces
27	 */
28	
29	export function stripMarkdownForFTS(markdown: string): string {
30	  let text = markdown;
31	
32	  // Remove code blocks (``` ... ```)
33	  text = text.replace(/```[\s\S]*?```/g, '');
34	
35	  // Remove inline code (`code`) — keep content
36	  text = text.replace(/`([^`]+)`/g, '$1');
37	
38	  // Remove images ![alt](url) — keep alt text
39	  text = text.replace(/!\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]+\)/g, '$1');
40	
41	  // Convert links [text](url) to just text
42	  text = text.replace(/\[([^\]]+)\]\([^)]+\)/g, '$1');
43	
44	  // Remove wikilinks [[ref]] — keep the ref text
45	  text = text.replace(/\[\[([^\]]+)\]\]/g, '$1');
46	
47	  // Remove heading markers (# ## ###)
48	  text = text.replace(/^#{1,6}\s+/gm, '');
49	
50	  // Remove bold/italic markers
51	  text = text.replace(/(\*\*|__)(.*?)\1/g, '$2');
52	  text = text.replace(/(\*|_)(.*?)\1/g, '$2');
53	
54	  // Remove horizontal rules
55	  text = text.replace(/^(-{3,}|_{3,}|\*{3,})$/gm, '');
56	
57	  // Remove blockquote markers
58	  text = text.replace(/^>\s+/gm, '');
59	
60	  // Remove list markers (-, *, +, 1.)
61	  text = text.replace(/^[\s]*[-*+]\s+/gm, '');
62	  text = text.replace(/^[\s]*\d+\.\s+/gm, '');
63	
64	  // Normalize whitespace
65	  return text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
66	}

1	/**
2	 * Extract `[[ref]]` wikilink targets from a Markdown body.
3	 *
4	 * Canonical implementation. Previously duplicated across:
5	 *   - routes/docs.ts         (POST /docs and PATCH wikilink replace)
6	 *   - routes/import.ts       (single-file import wikilink seed)
7	 *   - routes/import-bulk.ts  (Obsidian + Notion bulk import wikilink seed)
8	 *
9	 * 2 distinct hashes across the 3 copies — docs.ts kept a comment +
10	 * block-style `while { ... }`, the other two used an inline `while
11	 * ((m = re.exec(...))) out.push(...);`. Behaviourally equivalent;
12	 * extracted on 2026-05-18 (mirrors the stripMarkdownForFTS DRY in
13	 * 00e804a) so a future regex fix (e.g., allowing pipe-separated
14	 * aliases `[[ref|alias]]`) lands in one place.
15	 *
16	 * The current regex matches `[[<anything-not-]-or-newline>]]` and
17	 * returns the trimmed inner text. Pipe-aliases are NOT split — the
18	 * full `ref|alias` string is returned. If we ever support
19	 * alias-splitting, do it here and update the lib tests, not in the
20	 * route call sites.
21	 */
22	
23	export function extractWikilinks(markdown: string): string[] {
24	  // [[ref]] where ref can be a title or `/path`. The regex caps `]`
25	  // and `\n` so an unclosed `[[` doesn't run to end-of-doc and a
26	  // multi-line `]]` doesn't accidentally span lines.
27	  const out: string[] = [];
28	  const re = /\[\[([^\]\n]+)\]\]/g;
29	  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
30	  while ((m = re.exec(markdown)) !== null) {
31	    out.push(m[1].trim());
32	  }
33	  return out;
34	}
